key: ‘Remember now, O LORD, I beseech Thee, how I have walked before Thee in truth and with a whole heart, and have done that which is good in Thy sight.’ And Hezekiah wept sore.
s: Told by Isaiah that he will die, the sick Hezekiah turns to the wall and prays; Radak, on 20:3, reads ‘walked before Thee’ as the service of the heart, which he names first, and only then the deeds he has done.

evidence.gloss: I have walked before Thee: this is the service of the heart, and afterwards he mentioned the deed. … And have done that which is good in Thy sight: as Scripture testified of him, and he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as all that David his father had done.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 2 Kings 20:3 at [328,3] match. Radak on 20:3, lemma התהלכתי לפניך, says it is the service of the heart and that afterwards he mentioned the deed; his next lemma, on the good done, cites Scripture’s testimony to the deeds. The sentence gives heart first and deeds after, no more. Plain sense matches 20:1 to 20:2 (Isaiah’s word of death, the king turns to the wall and prays) with no four-word overlap. Rashi and Metzudat David say nothing on 20:3; Midrash empty. entry-check ok, no warns.
